note: PRE reproduced and frozen BEFORE any edit, against the categorical shape the owner-authorized read-only capture observed. The finding is mine, and it is the INVERSE of one already caught in the simulator: there an independent reversal passed for protection; here protection passed for an entry, and the wind-down would have cancelled it.

C9_1_recorded_shape_as_returned.message: alpaca.order[0]: unknown fields ['position_intent'] — an unrecognised field may carry meaning this parser does not model

PRE.verdict: the real payload did not parse at all, and the two 'clean it up first' steps that make it parse — strip the venue's own semantics, normalise null to an empty list — are exactly what produced the misclassification. A protective take-profit was read as an ENTRY.
PRE.geometry_would_also_be_wrong: a BUY standing against a SHORT looks exactly like a reversal, so side and quantity could not have rescued it either.

downstream_consequence_reproduced.meaning: WIND_DOWN would have offered the protective take-profit for cancellation while reporting a false pending entry.

role_from_declared_intent.rule: opening intents are entries; a closing bracket limit order is a protective take-profit; a closing bracket stop or stop-limit is a protective stop; anything else refuses. Side must agree with the intent's buy/sell half or the venue's own facts disagree and it refuses.

two_shapes_supported_explicitly.opening_intent_with_nested_legs: the object is the entry and each leg is protection typed by its own type
two_shapes_supported_explicitly.closing_intent_with_null_or_empty_legs: the object is itself the protective child
two_shapes_supported_explicitly.opening_intent_without_legs: refused — not a shape this parser models
two_shapes_supported_explicitly.closing_intent_carrying_legs: refused — a protective child has no children of its own
two_shapes_supported_explicitly.legs_of_any_other_kind: refused — must be null or a list

POST.no_normalisation_before_the_contract: asserted by a test that the parser source contains neither `legs or []` nor `legs = []`; null and [] reach the contract as the venue sent them.

self_reported_second_defect.found_by: my own WIND_DOWN assertions while writing this battery
self_reported_second_defect.claim: cancelling pending entries is a consequence of the session STATE, not of the model's command, but the adapter honoured decision['cancel_pending'] only inside the masked branch. A pending entry therefore survived WIND_DOWN whenever the model's command happened not to be risk-increasing.
self_reported_second_defect.fix: every branch now honours it, and the reason string says the cancellation follows from the state and not from the command.

POST.mutation_check: ignoring the declared intent and treating every bracket as an entry broke 69 tests across the evidence and adapter suites; the suites returned to green when reverted.
